$comment: Every non-shell screen in supplement.product.nutrition.json. Shell screens SH1–SH6 are deliberately absent: they are identical in every programme and are not this file's to write. The person throughout is Rosa, 46, a school-bus driver on a split shift; her sister Ana is her supporter and Priya is her coach. Every string is unreviewed.

S01.headline: No counting. No weigh-ins. No before and after.
S01.sub: OneChange works on one change at a time — small enough to keep on a bad week, and chosen by you rather than handed to you.

blocks.title: Nothing to log
blocks.body: No calorie counting, no food diary, no daily number to hit. Those aren't left out to be kind. They're left out because for most people they don't hold, and what doesn't hold isn't support.

blocks.title: There are no scales here
blocks.body: The programme never asks your weight, never draws it as a line, and never sets you beside anybody else.

blocks.title: A hard week stays in the record
blocks.body: Nothing resets, nothing is taken back, and nobody is told. A hard stretch is a fact about a week, not a verdict on you.

S01.footer: Education and self-management support. Not a diagnosis or treatment.

S02.title: What it does
S02.headline: Four moments this is built for.
S02.sub: Not four features. Four times this gets hard.

blocks.title: When you can't say where last week went
blocks.body: Two weeks of noticing, before anything changes. Minutes you moved, and where the hard part of the day actually sits. Nothing is scored and nothing is blocked.

blocks.title: When you're at the counter at nine at night
blocks.body: The one change you picked, in your own words, on the screen. Not a rule somebody else wrote for somebody else.

blocks.title: When the week goes badly
blocks.body: It goes in as history. Nothing zeroes, nobody is notified, and you are never asked to make it up afterwards.

blocks.title: When you want one person to know
blocks.body: One person you pick, who sees the small thing you decided to show them, on the day you send it.

blocks.title: What it isn't
blocks.body: It doesn't count anything you eat, set you a daily amount, weigh you, photograph your plate, or rank you against anyone.

S02.footer: Education and self-management support. Not a diagnosis or treatment.

S03.title: Consent & privacy
S03.headline: What we hold, and what we don't.

blocks.title: Held on your phone
blocks.body: The change you chose, your reasons, your notes, and the days you moved. These stay here.

blocks.title: Shared with your care team
blocks.body: Whether you're still going, and which changes you're holding. Never a note you wrote, never a photo, never anything about what you ate — because we never ask.

blocks.title: You can leave
blocks.body: Export or delete all of it at any point. Deletion is finished, not hidden, and it doesn't wait for anyone's approval.

items.title: Share my weekly summary with Priya

S03.footer: You can change either choice later in Settings.

S04.title: First two weeks
S04.headline: Just carry on as you are.
S04.sub: Nothing changes for two weeks. We're looking for where your day gets hard, and you're the one telling us — there is nothing to measure and nothing to submit.

blocks.title: Where it's getting hard
blocks.body: Between nine and ten at night, after the afternoon run. Four days out of four so far.
All of this is what you told us. OneChange measures nothing, reads nothing from your phone, and doesn't treat any of it as a clinical measurement.

blocks.title: You don't have to wait two weeks
blocks.body: Two weeks makes the picture better, not truer. Start your change now and we'll note the picture is partial.

S05.title: Choose your path
S05.headline: Change one thing, or change the shape of the day?
S05.sub: Neither is the better answer, and switching later costs you nothing.

items.title: Change one thing
items.body: One change, held until it stops taking effort. Most people start here.

items.title: Change the shape of the day
items.body: Not what's on the plate — when and where you eat it. Sitting down, and stopping at the table.

items.title: Start with your feet
items.body: Leave food alone for now and move a bit more first. Food changes tend to land better afterwards.

blocks.body: Whichever you pick, OneChange sets you no daily amount, asks you to log no meals, and never asks you to make up for a bad day.

S06.title: Your change
S06.headline: What's one thing you could hold on a bad week?
S06.sub: Not your best week. A bad one — a double shift, no sleep, Ana ill. That's the real test of a change.

items.title: Sit down to eat dinner
items.body: At the table, plate down, not at the counter with the kettle going.

items.title: Eat something before the afternoon run
items.body: So nine o'clock isn't the first proper sit-down of the day.

items.title: Walk the long way back from the depot
items.body: Ten minutes, the same route every time, no decision left to make.

blocks.title: How often, honestly?
blocks.body: Aim low. A change you keep four days a week beats one you abandon in a fortnight.
blocks.mid: Four or five days a week

blocks.title: When you'd want a nudge
blocks.body: Optional. A nudge is a reminder, not a check-up — nothing is recorded if you ignore it.

blocks.title: There is no number here on purpose
blocks.body: No daily target, no amount, no allowance. What the programme keeps is whether the change held — nothing about what was on the plate when it did.

S12.title: Your next step
S12.headline: One thing, not five.
S12.sub: Based on a long shift, a reach of 7, and dinner standing up.

blocks.title: Put a plate out before you leave for the afternoon run.
blocks.body: The counter wins at nine because the plate is three cupboards away. Move the effort to four in the afternoon, when it's cheap.

blocks.title: Or pick another
chips: Sit down for ten minutes first

blocks.body: Skipping is fine. We'll offer it again in a few days, and we won't ask why.

blocks.title: You ticked two harder ones today
blocks.body: There's a version of this programme with the counting switched off. It's there now, and it stays there whether you use it today or not.

S13.title: Fewer numbers
S13.headline: We're taking things away, not adding them.
S13.sub: You said food is taking up most of your thinking, and that you skipped meals to make up for yesterday. When we see that, the right move is less measuring, not tighter measuring. So this screen only offers to remove things.

blocks.title: Turn the counts off for a fortnight.
blocks.body: No minutes on your Today screen, no reach slider in the check-in, no weekly figures. The programme keeps running. You'll get one question a day — how was today — and that's the whole of it.

chips: Keep the check-in, drop the slider

blocks.title: This one is worth saying out loud to a person
blocks.body: Priya is a coach, not a clinician, so we don't leave it with her. She can put you in front of your care team this week, and 988 answers at any hour if tonight is a bad one.

blocks.title: Why this screen exists
blocks.body: An app that answers this with a stricter plan, a tighter number or a longer streak makes things worse, and plenty do. Ours is built to get quieter. That's the whole design, and it isn't a punishment — nothing is being withheld from you, and you can turn any of it back on.

blocks.title: Not now is a complete answer
blocks.body: Nothing changes if you close this, nothing is recorded about it, and we won't ask why. The offer sits in Settings from now on.

S13.footer: Turning anything back on is one tap in Settings, whenever you want it.

S14.title: A hard stretch

blocks.title: A hard week is a fact about a week.
blocks.body: Both your changes are still held, week 5 is still week 5, and last week stays in the chart exactly as it happened. Nothing below deletes, rewinds or zeroes any of it.

items.title: A couple of evenings got away from me

blocks.title: What was going on?
blocks.body: Optional. It moves what we suggest next, and nothing else.

blocks.title: What now
blocks.body: Nothing to make up. There's no deficit here to pay back, and we are not going to ask you to eat less this week because of last week.

blocks.title: Start again at dinner tonight, not on Monday.
blocks.body: The changes that come back the same evening are the ones that stay. Waiting for a clean start is what turns two evenings into three weeks.

S14.footer: Saves offline and syncs once · You can delete this event later

S15.title: Your kitchen
S15.headline: Make the nine o'clock reach harder to do.
S15.sub: Each of these lowers how often the reach starts. None of them ask you to resist anything.

blocks.title: Fewer reaches beats more resisting.
blocks.body: Most evenings don't begin with a decision. They begin with a cupboard at eye level and a plate three cupboards away. Move those two things and the decision never comes up.

blocks.title: Swap the eye-level shelf with the top one.
blocks.body: Ten minutes, once. The honest cost: the things you actually cook with are now up high too, and you'll be cross about it for a week.

blocks.title: Put the plate out in the afternoon
blocks.body: Before the run, not after it. Costs nothing at four and saves you the whole walk at nine.

blocks.title: Do the Wednesday shop on the way back, not the way out
blocks.body: After the afternoon run rather than before it. The cost is twenty minutes in a colder bus and no second trip if you forget something.

blocks.title: Eat at the table, phone in the hall
blocks.body: The hardest of the four, and the one people keep longest. The cost is real: you'll miss calls during dinner, including Ana's.

items: Ask once, and remember what you said
Photograph, count or inspect anything in your kitchen
You. Ana sees none of this unless you send it.

blocks.title: All of it is yours to undo
blocks.body: Every change here is one you make with your own hands in your own house. Putting the shelf back takes ten minutes and doesn't need us, or this app, or anyone's permission. If we ever couldn't hand something back, we wouldn't offer it.

S15.footer: Nothing here is checked up on. We only ever know what you tell us.
